name: mysqlpeek
description: Read-only MySQL and MariaDB access for one or many instances. Explore schemas, cost a query with EXPLAIN before running it, and pick the instance per call. Writes are refused by the database engine itself, not only by a parser.

MYSQL_HOST.title: Server
MYSQL_HOST.description: db.internal, host:port, or mysql://host:3306 (mysqls:// for TLS). Port defaults to 3306. Leave empty if you use a profiles file instead.

MYSQL_USER.title: Username
MYSQL_USER.description: Use an account granted only SELECT (plus PROCESS and REPLICATION CLIENT for the ops tools). The grant is the layer that can actually enforce read-only.

MYSQL_PASSWORD.title: Password
MYSQL_PASSWORD.description: Stored in your system keychain, never in a settings file. Preserved across plugin updates.

MYSQL_DATABASE.title: Database (optional)
MYSQL_DATABASE.description: Used when a tool call does not name one. Leave empty to require every call to say.

MYSQLPEEK_PROFILES.title: Profiles file (optional, for several instances)
MYSQLPEEK_PROFILES.description: Path to a JSON file describing one or more instances. Takes precedence over the fields above. Use it when you have more than one server, or when credentials come from a secret manager: the file holds ${env:...}, ${file:...} or ${cmd:...} references rather than values, so it is safe to commit.
